messages:
alex: Following up on the AuthN/AuthZ RFC — proposal to add project-scoped API keys + a dedicated service token type. TL;DR: keep org-level keys for admin/backcompat, but default to project-scoped keys, and introduce short-lived service tokens (1h TTL) + optional mTLS for svc->svc. Looking for tradeoffs and migration plans.

maya: +1 on project scope. worried about key sprawl though. how do we keep UX simple for devs? :thinking:

alex: Good call. Proposal includes a single dashboard view that groups keys by project and by issuer, with filters. Also a CLI to list keys by project. Aim to auto-expire unused keys after 90 days (opt-outable).

tj: From RBAC side, recommend we avoid per-resource ACLs initially. Start with role-based perms at project level: owner, editor, reader, service. Keep rules simple so policy eval is fast.

sean: How do service tokens differ from API keys in terms of capabilities? e.g., can a service token be limited to embeddings only?

alex: Yes. Service tokens support a scope set (generation, embeddings, rerank) and optional ip_cidr and allowed_models. Example token metadata: 
```
{
  "type": "service",
  "scopes": ["generation"],
  "project": "payments",
  "ttl": 3600
}
```
This lets infra issue tokens for specific pipelines.

maya: We should add an audit field so tokens record the issuing principal and the request id for creation. Also record key rotations in audit logs.

tj: What about token validation perf? We need to avoid a DB hop per request. Suggest signed JWTs for service tokens with short TTL validated via local public key cache; API keys can be looked up in KV cache.

alex: Agreed. Plan: service tokens = JWT (signed by token-service), rotated public keys via key-distribution; API keys remain opaque IDs mapped to metadata cached in memcache layer for hot keys.

sean: For mobile or browser-embedded use cases, we still need limited client tokens. Propose "client tokens" with granular scopes + origin restriction + 1d TTL. Not for admin ops.

maya: Migration notes: we need backwards compatibility for existing org keys. Proposal: introduce prefix flavors: org_*, proj_*, svc_*. Support both for 12 months and emit deprecation warnings in logs/console.

alex: Migration CLI sketch: 
```
# migrate keys from org -> project default
redwood keys migrate --org old-org --default-project prod --dry-run
```
We'll also emit advisory emails to admins before enforced changes.

tj: Security tradeoff: JWTs prevent DB lookups but make revocation trickier. We'll implement a short revocation list keyed by jti in Redis for emergency revokes, and rely on short TTLs for normal lifecycle. Documented in RFC.

sean: Ops question: How will this interact with Dedicated/Private deployments where KMS is customer-managed? We need an option to sign tokens with customer key in private mode.

alex: Yes, plan is to allow customer KMS/HSM to sign service tokens in Private deployments; token issuer endpoint will be configured to use customer keyring. We'll have a fallthrough to Redwood signer for hosted.

ops-bot: deploy-check: authz-service unit tests: 14 failed, see CI link https://ci.internal/1234

maya: I'll take test triage. Most failures look like policy-eval edge cases around project-less keys.

alex: Action items: 1) tj to write policy-eval perf tests (due EOW), 2) maya to draft migration announcement + console deprecation warnings, 3) sean to spec client-token origin restrictions and SDK changes, 4) infra to add public key rotation endpoint. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with these decisions. Any objections? :lock: 

tj: No objections. prefer clear docs on revocation. :+1:

sean: no objections, want a small experiment enabling project-scoped keys for a single beta org first.

maya: agreed, will coordinate beta.

alex: thanks all — I'll post the RFC follow-up and link it here when ready.
